newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BOKSIC SENT OFF BUT JUVENTUS HOLD INTER 0-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOKSIC SENT OFF BUT JUVENTUS HOLD INTER 0-0.

text.p: Alen Boksic was sent off on his return to Serie A after a two-month lay-off on Sunday but 10-man Juventus still held title rivals Inter Milan to a 0-0 draw at the San Siro.
The result kept the league leaders on course for a record 24th league title, although second-placed Parma have cut their lead at the top to five points, having won 2-1 at Perugia earlier.
Croatian forward Boksic was dismissed in the 77th minute for striking Inter defender Massimo Paganin just 10 minutes after coming on as a second-half substitute.
But the match had turned on another controversial incident in the seventh minute when Maurizio Ganz, clearly off-side, was allowed to play on and beat Angelo Peruzzi at the second attempt.
Referee Pierluigi Collina first pointed to the halfway line to signal a goal but then changed his mind, ruling out a goal.
As whistles rang out round the ground and Inter players surrounded Collina, the referee walked to the sidelines to admit his mistake to manager Roy Hodgson.
"I've never seen anything like it in 45 years of football," said an angry Inter president Massimo Moratti after the match.
The decision also rattled Moratti's players who rarely looked in control for the remainder of the first half.
Straight after the disallowed goal, Juventus striker Nicola Amoruso took advantage of some shaky Inter defending with a shot which deflected off Gianluca Pagliuca's body on to the post.
After the break Italy's former number one goalkeeper Pagliuca and current incumbent Peruzzi together insured the scoresheet remained blank with a series of fine saves.
In the 70th minute, Peruzzi went full-length to turn Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff's shot round the post while Pagliuca saved bravely at the feet of striker Christian Vieri.
Despite Boksic's dismissal, the draw was far more damaging to Inter than Juventus: Hodgson's side remained seven points behind the leaders with their title hopes looking increasingly remote.
Parma, who came from behind to defeat Perugia, now look like the only club capable of stopping Juventus -- but manager Carlo Ancelotti is reluctant to take up the challenge.
"In terms of points, the title races is still wide open," said Ancelotti, whose team have lost only once this year.
"But in terms of potential, Juventus cannot be caught."
Instead, Parma prefer to set their sights on the runners-up spot which now guarantees a lucrative European Cup place.
Parma reacted with clinical efficiency to falling behind in the 11th minute.
Within a minute Argentine Hernan Crespo equalised with his third goal in two matches and five minutes later Massimo Crippa scored the winner with a powerful shot from the edge of the area.
Sampdoria's faltering title challenge suffered a devastating 4-0 blow at Atalanta.
Atalanta's Filippo Inzaghi, the league's leading scorer, ran rings around Sampdoria's suspect defence to claim a hat-trick and take his season's tally to 18.
Sampdoria's Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic was dismissed after he threw the ball at the referee when Atalanta were given a penalty.
Fourth-placed Sampdoria, who have taken just one point in ther last four matches, are nine points adrift of Juventus.
Until last week's European Cup Winners' quarter-final first leg win at Benfica, Fiorentina had failed to win in two months.
And when Swede Kennet Andersson put Bologna in front in the second minute, their miserable league record looked like continuing.
Even when Fiorentina levelled with an 18th-minute Francesco Baiano penalty, Aldo Firicano promptly deflected Carlo Nervo's shot into his own net to restore Bologna's lead.

But in an inspired second half, two superb free-kicks converted first by Gabriele Batisuta, then Anselmo Robbiati, brought Fiorentina a long-awaited victory -- marred only by the sending-off of Swede Stefan Schwarz.
French defender Vincent Candela lifted Roma into fifth place with two goals, including a dramatic 89th-minute winner, in his side's 4-3 win over bottom-placed Verona at the Olympic stadium.

Napoli fans greeted AC Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi by throwing a black rubbish bag on to the pitch. The gesture summed up Milan's visit fittingly -- a dull scoreless draw which left the champions languishing in 12th place without an away win in 1997.
